text:
ryan_support: heads up — ACME reported vectors/sec drop ~60% starting 09:10 UTC. tokens/sec unchanged. they see 200ms token latency ok but vecs piling up, p95 vec latency spikes. trace id: trace-0a7b. can infra take a look?

jess_devops: looking. any auth/billing errors in the logs?

ryan_support: no 4xx in customer logs. they hit 200s 429s? nope. only 200s but throughput low. customer says embedding dims still 1536. they sent batched 128 requests earlier.

mike_infra: pulling queue metrics now — kvcache queue depth on shard s-12 went from ~20 -> 280 at 09:11 UTC. GPU utilization stayed ~70%. interesting.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout "batch-window-adjustment" to service embeddings-svc completed at 09:08 UTC (rev 2026-03-17-18).

jess_devops: that rollout changed batch_window_ms from 15 -> 6 to reduce latency. we suspected smaller windows might reduce batching efficiency.

ryan_support: so smaller window -> more, smaller batches -> overhead -> vectors/sec drop? but tokens/sec unaffected? seems odd.

tanya_ml: quick theory: reducing batch window reduces average batch size for embeddings which increases per-request kernel overhead and increases arrival-to-dequeue churn; also may cause more KV cache thrashing if more concurrent requests touch different prefixes. that would lower vec tokens/sec even if tokenization stage is same.

mike_infra: copying relevant snippet from metrics (09:05 -> 09:20):
```
metric: vecs/sec per shard
s-12: 1300 -> 470
s-13: 1400 -> 420
avg batch size: 12 -> 4
gpu queue depth: 18 -> 270
kv_lock_wait_ms: p95 6ms -> 180ms
```

sam_oncall: saw increased queue backpressure and retries in routing. routing logs show many small batches being enqueued which bog down the continuous_batcher.

jess_devops: can we reproduce locally? tanya, can you run a sim with batch window 6 vs 15 using current traffic mix? use this load script:
```
# run locally
python tools/loadgen.py --profile=acme-embedding --concurrency=120 --qps=240 --batch_window_ms=6
# compare with --batch_window_ms=15
```

tanya_ml: running now, will post numbers but early result: vectors/sec drops ~58% with window 6. CPU on host scheduler higher, kernel launch rate doubled.

ryan_support: ACME is on Dedicated pool d-acme-w1. can we roll them back to previous config while we investigate?

mike_infra: we can pin their routing to rev-2026-03-17-17 (pre-rollout) for dedicated pools. initiating rollback for d-acme-w1 -> will take ~30s to drain in-progress.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: traffic pin initiated for customer acme -> routing pinned to rev-2026-03-17-17 at 09:22 UTC by mike_infra.

sam_oncall: temporary mitigation applied. monitor p95 vec latency and vecs/sec.

tanya_ml: follow-up: need a guard in the rollout that prevents batch_window_ms < X when average batch size falls below threshold for embeddings workloads. also add telemetry to surface batch size distribution per customer.

jess_devops: agreed. filing infra ticket and a product config constraint. repo links: https://git.redwood/inference/rollouts/issues/1421

ryan_support: customer updated: "throughput back to normal after rollback, thanks!" :thumbsup:

mike_infra: logging post-rollback metrics: s-12 vecs/sec returned to ~1280 within 60s. GPU queue depth normalized.

tanya_ml: proposed postmortem notes: root cause = aggressive batch_window tuning -> unintended batch fragmentation -> KV lock wait increased -> throughput regression for vectors. mitigations: revert rollout, add rollout guard, add per-customer batch-size telemetry, and an automatic fallback to previous batch config when vecs/sec drops > 30% for 2 consecutive minutes.

ryan_support: creating support ticket and linking to incident. will follow up with customer summary and RCA draft.

jess_devops: thanks all. I'll escalate to release team to prevent similar short-window rollouts to embedding paths without perf gates.

sam_oncall: adding note: also check billing signals — if batch reduction increases per-token cost unexpectedly, alert finance/product.
